stimulus.source_note: Photograph: crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival, August 15, 1969, by Derek Redmond and Paul Campbell, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Attendance figures verified against Britannica and the Smithsonian; Altamont account verified against Britannica and Library of Congress accounts.
stimulus.text:
The photograph, taken on August 15, 1969, shows part of the huge crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York. More than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of rock music. The promoters had told local officials to expect no more than 50,000 people.

Four months later, in December 1969, promoters tried to repeat Woodstock with a free festival at the Altamont Speedway in California. The event was disorganized, the Hells Angels motorcycle club served as security, and a concertgoer, Meredith Hunter, was stabbed and killed during the Rolling Stones’ set.

stem: Woodstock in August 1969 and Altamont in December 1969 together best show which of the following?

options.text: The counterculture had already disappeared by 1969
options.misconception: Woodstock alone drew more than 400,000 people in 1969.

options.text: The counterculture reached its peak and showed its limits in the same year
Rock festivals were banned by the federal government after Altamont in 1969
options.misconception: Background: No federal ban on festivals followed Altamont.

options.text: Young people lost all interest in rock music after 1969
options.misconception: Background: Rock stayed popular through the 1970s.

rationales.A: Background: Both festivals drew huge crowds in 1969, so the counterculture had not disappeared.
rationales.B: Background: Woodstock gathered more than 400,000 people in peace; four months later Altamont ended in disorganization and a killing. The same year held the peak and the limit.
rationales.C: Background: No federal ban on rock festivals followed Altamont. Festivals continued into the 1970s.
rationales.D: Background: Rock music stayed popular through the 1970s. Altamont did not end it.
rationales.general:
1. Woodstock drew more than 400,000 young people for three days of music.
2. Altamont, four months later, was disorganized and ended with a killing.
3. The two festivals are the same movement at its largest and at its most troubled.
4. A peak and a limit in one year is a turning point, not a disappearance.
Remember: Compare the high point and the low point together: the gap between them is the story.
